## 2. Slide-by-Slide Content & Speaker Notes

### Slide 1 — Title & Problem Scope (0:20)
- **On-Slide Elements:**
  - Course: SENG435 Digital Image Processing
  - Title: *Intelligent Solar Cell Defect Classification Using Genetic Algorithm-Based Feature Selection*
  - Scope Strip: ELPV Electroluminescence Benchmark (`2,223` binary cells) | Classical HOG + LBP (`334` -> `208` features) | LinearSVC with a held-out cell-level test split
- **Speaker Notes:**
  - Automated inspection of electroluminescence (EL) photovoltaic cell imagery detects micro-cracks and dark-area defects quickly without heavy deep models.
  - Instead of trusting all `334` handcrafted texture and edge descriptors blindly, we pair classical HOG + LBP features with a Genetic Algorithm (GA) wrapper to compact the representation while preserving defect detection quality.

### Slide 2 — Dataset & Strict Anti-Leakage Protocol (0:25)
- **On-Slide Elements:**
  - ELPV raw corpus: `2,624` grayscale 300x300 cells (`1,074` mono, `1,550` poly).
  - Binary subset (`2,223` cells): `1,508` HEALTHY (`0.0`), `715` DEFECTIVE (`1.0`); `401` uncertain labels (`0.3333`, `0.6667`) excluded cleanly.
  - Frozen stratified split (`data/splits.csv`, `seed=42`): Train `1,556` (`1,056` / `500`), Val `333` (`226` / `107`), Test `334` (`226` / `108`).
  - Anti-leakage: `StandardScaler` lives inside `sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline`; `test` split locked exclusively for final E1–E5 reporting.
  - **Visual:** `results/figures/dataset_samples.png`
- **Speaker Notes:**
  - We restrict to clear binary consensus labels (`0.0` vs `1.0`) and freeze our stratified split early in `data/splits.csv`.
  - Notice `has_module_id=false` in the distributed dataset metadata: cells from the same module may appear in different partitions. Scaling parameters are fitted inside the training folds.

### Slide 3 — Classical Image Processing Features: HOG + LBP (0:30)
- **On-Slide Elements:**
  - Standardized input resolution: `64x64` grayscale.
  - **HOG (`324` dims):** `9` orientations, `16x16` pixels/cell, `2x2` cells/block (`L2-Hys`, `3x3` overlapping blocks) — captures directional crack edges and busbar geometry.
  - **LBP (`10` dims):** `P=8`, `R=1`, `method="uniform"` — captures isotropic micro-grain and surface dark-area textures.
  - Total concatenated vector: `334` dims (`2.8554 s` for all `2,223` images = `1.2845 ms/image`).
  - **Visual:** `results/figures/feature_visualization.png` (`cell0004` HEALTHY vs `cell0001` DEFECTIVE, mono).
- **Speaker Notes:**
  - Cracks produce strong local oriented gradients (captured by HOG), whereas shunts and inactive dark spots alter micro-texture histograms (captured by uniform LBP).
  - Combining both yields a `334`-dimensional CPU-friendly descriptor extracted in just over `1.28 ms` per image.

### Slide 4 — Intelligent Technique: Genetic Algorithm Feature Selection (0:30)
- **On-Slide Elements:**
  - Chromosome representation: `334`-bit binary mask `m` (`1` = keep feature, `0` = drop).
  - Parsimony-aware fitness on **Train 3-fold stratified CV only**:
    `fitness(m) = CV_Macro_F1(m) - lambda * (sum(m) / 334)` with `lambda = 0.05`.
  - GA config: `population_size=12`, `generations=8`, two-point crossover (`p=0.7`), bit-flip mutation (`1/334 = 0.002994`), elitism (`2`), tournament (`k=3`).
  - Result (`seed=42`): `8.177 s` search (`82` unique evals, `26` cache hits); best fitness rises from Gen 0 to `0.7123` (`CV Macro F1 = 0.7434 ± 0.0117`).
  - **Visual:** `results/figures/ga_convergence.png`
- **Speaker Notes:**
  - Using a GA wrapper lets the solver jointly evaluate subsets of correlated HOG blocks and LBP bins while directly penalizing dimensionality with `lambda=0.05`.
  - Memoization caches repeated masks across generations (`26` hits), keeping single-seed search under `8.2` seconds on CPU.

### Slide 5 — Selected Feature Breakdown: `208 / 334` Retained (0:25)
- **On-Slide Elements:**
  - Overall reduction: `334` -> `208` features (`-37.72%`).
  - By family (`seed=42`): HOG `198 / 324` (`61.1%` kept) vs **LBP `10 / 10` (`100.0%` kept)**.
  - Mean across 3 GA seeds (`42, 123, 999`): `184.67 / 324` HOG vs `8.00 / 10` LBP (`42.31%` overall dimensionality reduction).
  - **Visual:** `results/figures/selected_features_breakdown.png`
- **Speaker Notes:**
  - Remarkably, without any domain prior, the GA retained **all 10/10 uniform LBP bins** on seed `42` and averaged `8/10` across seeds, while pruning `126` redundant HOG dimensions.
  - On this split the combined descriptor scored above either descriptor alone.

### Slide 6 — Baseline Tuning & Master E1–E5 Comparison (0:35)
- **On-Slide Elements:**
  - Baseline validation grid (`balanced, C=0.001` vs `C=1.0`): strong regularization jumps Validation Macro F1 from `0.6848` -> `0.7635` (Defective Recall `0.7103`).
  - Master locked-test comparison table (`n=334`):
    - **E1 Baseline (334):** Test Macro F1 `0.7258`, Def F1 `0.6372`, Def Rec `0.6667`, Acc `0.7545`, Fit `0.1055 s`
    - **E2 GA-SVM seed 42 (208, -37.72%):** Test Macro F1 **`0.7325`**, Def F1 **`0.6460`**, Def Rec **`0.6759`**, Acc **`0.7605`**, Fit `0.0618 s`
    - **E2 GA 3-seed mean (192.67, -42.31%):** Test Macro F1 `0.7232`, Def F1 `0.6331`, Def Rec `0.6605`, Acc `0.7525`
    - **E3 HOG-Only (324):** Test Macro F1 `0.7045`, Def Rec `0.6296`, Acc `0.7365`
    - **E4 LBP-Only (10):** Test Macro F1 `0.6949`, Def Rec `0.7037`, Def Prec `0.5468`, Acc `0.7156`
    - **E5 Random-208 (5-seed mean):** Test Macro F1 `0.7151`, Def Rec `0.6685`, Acc `0.7425`
- **Speaker Notes:**
  - Three takeaways emerge directly from this ablation matrix:
    1. Regularizing LinearSVC (`C=0.001`, `balanced`) gave the highest validation Macro F1 among the tested settings.
    2. E2 (`seed=42`) beats E1 on every locked test metric using `37.72%` fewer features, and outperforms HOG-only (E3), LBP-only (E4), and size-matched Random-208 (E5).
    3. LBP-only reaches high recall (`0.7037`) only at the cost of low precision (`0.5468`); HOG + LBP fusion fixes that false-alarm problem.

### Slide 7 — Multi-Seed Stability & Honest Trade-off Analysis (0:25)
- **On-Slide Elements:**
  - Multi-seed table (`GA` across seeds `42, 123, 999`):
    - `seed=42`: `208` feats (`198/10`), `-37.72%`, Fitness `0.7123`, Test Macro F1 `0.7325`, Search `7.3563 s`
    - `seed=123`: `215` feats (`207/8`), `-35.63%`, Fitness `0.7139`, Test Macro F1 `0.7179`, Search `6.5769 s`
    - `seed=999`: `155` feats (`149/6`), `-53.59%`, Fitness `0.7285`, Test Macro F1 `0.7191`, Search `4.9482 s`
    - Mean ± Std: `192.67 ± 32.81` feats (`42.31 ± 9.82%` red), Test Macro F1 `0.7232 ± 0.0081`, Acc `0.7525 ± 0.0069`.
  - Honest trade-off note:
    - Why does `seed=999` score higher fitness (`0.7285`) yet slightly lower test F1 (`0.7191`)? Aggressive `lambda=0.05` rewards dropping down to `155` features, trimming some marginal discriminatory cues alongside noise.
- **Speaker Notes:**
  - Reporting only seed `42` would hide stochastic GA variance, so we run 3 independent seeds.
  - Across seeds, GA achieves comparable generalization (`0.7232` vs E1 `0.7258`, within `-0.0026`) while removing `42.31%` of features on average, and consistently beating Random-208 (`0.7151`).

### Slide 8 — Confusion Matrices & Error Analysis (Mono vs Poly) (0:30)
- **On-Slide Elements:**
  - Confusion counts (`test=334`): E1 `TP=72, TN=180, FP=46, FN=36` (`82` errors) -> E2 `TP=73, TN=181, FP=45, FN=35` (`80` errors; `20` disagreements: `11` fixed, `9` regressed).
  - Error rate by wafer type:
    - Monocrystalline (`n=135`): E1 `20` errors (`14.81%`), E2 `24` errors (`17.78%`).
    - Polycrystalline (`n=199`): E1 `62` errors (`31.16%`), E2 `56` errors (`28.14%`).
  - **Visuals:** `results/figures/confusion_matrices.png` & `results/figures/error_analysis_grid.png`
- **Speaker Notes:**
  - Polycrystalline cells suffer roughly double the error rate of monocrystalline cells because natural crystalline grain boundaries visually mimic micro-crack gradients and dark regions, driving false positives and false negatives.
  - Still, GA selection yields a net `+2` reduction in test errors (`82` -> `80`), mostly by suppressing polycrystalline false alarms (`62` -> `56` poly errors).

- ELPV labels identify crystal type but omit module identifiers. The cell-level split can include cells from the same module in different partitions.

## 4. Expected Instructor / Peer Q&A Defense Guide

1. **Q: Why did you exclude the 401 images with probabilities `0.3333` and `0.6667`?**
   - *A:* In ELPV, labels represent expert-rater consensus. `0.3333` and `0.6667` correspond to 1-of-3 or 2-of-3 annotator disagreement. For supervised binary evaluation (`E1–E5`), restricting to unanimous `0.0` (`1,508`) and `1.0` (`715`) labels (`2,223` total) prevents annotator label noise from distorting Macro F1 and confusion matrices, while leaving uncertain-label filtering documented as future work (ordinal/soft labeling).

2. **Q: Since `has_module_id=false` in ELPV, could same-module cells appear in both train and test?**
   - *A:* Yes, and we explicitly audit and disclose `has_module_id=false` in `results/dataset_summary.json`, our report, and Slide 2. Because the distributed ELPV metadata lacks solar module identifiers, a strict GroupKFold by module is impossible without external labeling. We therefore enforced strict `StandardScaler` fitting inside CV/train pipelines only and kept the stratified `test` split (`334` images) untouched throughout all tuning and GA evolution.

3. **Q: Why did `LinearSVC` use `C=0.001` with `class_weight="balanced"` instead of default `C=1.0`?**
   - *A:* The binary subset is imbalanced (`~2.11:1`, `1,508` healthy vs `715` defective). On our validation grid (`results/baseline_validation_grid.csv`), default unregularized/weakly regularized `C=1.0` overfit noisy background gradients (`Val Macro F1 = 0.6848`), whereas strong L2 regularization (`C=0.001`) + balanced class weights jumped `Val Macro F1` to `0.7635` and `Val Defective Recall` to `0.7103`.

4. **Q: Why did the GA keep `10/10` LBP bins on `seed=42` (`8.0/10` mean across seeds) while dropping ~`126–175` HOG bins?**
   - *A:* Each `10`-bin Uniform LBP vector (`P=8, R=1, method="uniform"`) is already compact and summarizes micro-texture grain/dark-spot distributions globally, so dropping any bin loses unique histogram support (`E4` LBP-only still reaches `0.7037` defective recall). Meanwhile, adjacent `16x16` HOG cells on outer borders or uniform wafer interiors carry correlated/redundant gradient information that L2 linear SVM and GA can prune safely.

5. **Q: Are the `+1.6783` or `-0.2085` numbers on your demo output probabilities?**
   - *A:* LinearSVC returns an uncalibrated decision score with a threshold of zero. Positive values indicate a defective prediction. Values at or below zero indicate a healthy prediction. Probabilities would require separate calibration.

6. **Q: Why does GA `seed=999` have higher CV fitness (`0.7285`) than `seed=42` (`0.7123`), yet lower locked-test Macro F1 (`0.7191` vs `0.7325`)?**
   - *A:* Seed 999 used 155 features and obtained a higher training CV Macro F1. Its smaller subset also incurred a lower feature-count penalty. Its lower result on the held-out cells is an observation about these runs.

7. **Q: Why is polycrystalline error (`28.14%` on E2) almost double monocrystalline error (`17.78%` on E2)?**
   - *A:* Monocrystalline wafers have uniform dark silicon backgrounds, so crack edges stand out sharply in HOG gradients. Polycrystalline wafers contain natural multi-grain boundaries with varying crystallographic reflectance that produce cluttered high-frequency gradient edges indistinguishable from hairline cracks at `64x64` HOG resolution.
